URL: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/rachel-reeves-cost-of-living-package-payment-b2981180.html
TITLE: What's included in Reeves' cost of living plan, what isn't – and who will really benefit?
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-21 13:30
AUTHOR: David Maddox (Political Editor)
SOURCE: The Independent

KEY MEASURES ANNOUNCED IN COMMONS TODAY:

1. **MILEAGE RATE: 10p increase to 55p** (from 45p)
   - Backdated to April 2026
   - First raise in 15 years (Osborne raised 40p→45p)
   - "Biggest help in the measures"; aimed at "white van man" — workers using vehicles for work
   - Significantly helps offset costs against tax

2. **FUEL DUTY** (announced Wednesday): 5p cut extended through end of 2026

3. **VAT cut on summer attraction tickets: 20% → 5%**
   - Theme parks, zoos, museums
   - Caveat: "not a lot when cost of some tickets are north of £80"
   - Also VAT cut on children's meals

4. **Free bus travel for children over summer holiday** (already trailed)

5. **Removed tariffs from 100 imported food items** including biscuits, baked beans

6. **£120 MILLION CERAMICS INDUSTRY PACKAGE** for Stoke-on-Trent
   - Politically significant: Reform vs Labour battleground
   - Boris Johnson Tories won Stoke 2019; Labour won back 2024
   - Now Reform "set to sweep the area"
   - Ceramics also important for aerospace sector

MISSING/AVOIDED:
- Supermarket food price cap (dropped this week after retail backlash)
- Energy bill cap (avoided — "almost certainly because she could not afford it"; Truss precedent)

REEVES'S DEFENSE:
- "Fundamentals are right"
- IMF "upgraded the low forecast on growth"

INDEPENDENT FRAMING (David Maddox):
- "Proof of life for a government which many think is dead"
- "One last chance by Ms Reeves to give this government a political boost"
- "PM could be replaced before the summer and his chancellor Ms Reeves will surely follow him out of the exit door"
- "Uncertainty ties the hands of ministers in attempting to do anything significant"
- "In some ways an attempt by Ms Reeves to validate her economic legacy as change approaches"

PLUMBER OBSESSION FRAMING:
- Westminster's "obsession with plumbers"
- Green plumber Hannah Spencer won Gorton & Denton by-election
- Reform's plumber Robert Kenyon now Makerfield candidate vs Burnham
- Reeves "name-checked plumbers" in the announcement
